Reading passage:
Software testing has evolved from a manual, repetitive activity into a discipline that relies heavily on automation.
Automated tests can run thousands of checks overnight, giving developers quick feedback on every change. Yet
automation is not a magic cure. Poorly designed scripts break whenever the interface changes, and teams then
spend more time repairing tests than writing new ones. Experienced engineers therefore automate only stable,
high-value scenarios and leave exploratory work, which depends on human curiosity, to manual testers.

What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Automation has replaced all manual testing
Automation is valuable but should be applied selectively

Reading passage:
Large language models generate text by predicting likely words, not by looking up verified facts. As a result, they
can produce confident answers that are completely wrong, a problem often called hallucination. Testing such
systems is different from testing traditional software because the same question can yield slightly different
answers each time. Testers therefore design evaluation sets, check answers against trusted sources and look
for biased or unsafe outputs. No single test can guarantee perfect behaviour.

According to the passage, why do language models hallucinate?
options: They are connected to the internet
They predict likely words rather than look up verified facts

transfer that debits one account but fails to credit another leaves the books unbalanced. Database testers
therefore verify that data remains accurate, consistent and complete after every operation. They write queries to
compare stored values with expected results, check that rules such as unique account numbers are enforced
and ensure that failed transactions are rolled back cleanly.

It also distinguishes a temporary difference from a permanent imbalance. This requires tests to examine both individual records and aggregate balances rather than relying on a single response code.

Why define an expected consistency window?
options: To permit any delay without investigation
To distinguish an acceptable delay from a persistent inconsistency
To guarantee that every event arrives immediately

questions.question:

A bank’s reconciliation process compares records produced by systems that may update at different times. A mismatch immediately after a transfer does not always prove that money was lost; it may indicate that one system has not yet received an event. But repeatedly widening the acceptable delay can conceal a genuine defect. A sound test defines the expected consistency window, checks that delayed events are eventually applied, and verifies that replaying an event does not apply the same transfer twice. It also distinguishes a temporary difference from a permanent imbalance. This requires tests to examine both individual records and aggregate balances rather than relying on a single response code.

What risk can event replay create?
options: A transfer may be applied more than once.
An API response may become XML.
A test may use the wrong browser.

questions.question: The list of unresolved incidents, / together with the follow-up actions, / were circulated before the review.
Between you and I, / the revised test plan / is still incomplete.

options: that the intermittent failures are related to load

questions.question: Scarcely had the operator approved the batch / than the audit alert / appeared on the monitoring screen.
options: Scarcely had the operator approved the batch

questions.question: Each of the devices / have been registered / before the mobile test run.
Choose the word closest in meaning to mitigate.
Choose the word opposite in meaning to explicit.
Choose the word closest in meaning to tenable.
Choose the word opposite in meaning to sporadic.

options: unaware of Fill in the blank (Q21–25)

questions.question: The test lead insisted ___ preserving the original failure logs.
Had the API contract been reviewed earlier, the breaking change ___ before deployment.
The number of tests that ___ the new payment workflow has doubled.
The reconciliation job had completed, ___ the mismatch remained unexplained.
The candidate is responsible ___ reviewing the test evidence before sign-off.
A React page replaces a results row after an asynchronous update. A previously located WebElement now throws StaleElementReferenceException. What is the strongest fix?
options: Increase the implicit wait and reuse the same reference.
Re-locate the row after waiting for the updated state.
Catch the exception and treat the old reference as current.
Replace all element checks with JavaScript.

questions.question: A browser session uses the eager page-load strategy. Navigation returns before a client-side table has finished fetching and rendering its data. What should the test do?
options: Assume eager waits for all network activity to stop.
Switch to normal because it guarantees all later API calls are complete.
Wait explicitly for the table’s required state or data.
Add an implicit wait, which waits for the entire page to finish rendering.

questions.question: Selenium reports that a click is intercepted. The target is visible and enabled, but a loading overlay covers it. What should the test do?
options: Wait for the overlay to become invisible, then click.
Repeatedly click until one attempt succeeds.
Increase the implicit wait; it guarantees overlays disappear.
Pass the test because the target was visible.

questions.question: A dropdown visually resembles a standard select, but inspection shows it is a custom <div> menu. What is the correct approach?
options: Wrap it in Selenium’s Select class.
Use selectByVisibleText() on the parent container.
Send keys to an unrelated hidden <select>.
Interact with the menu using its actual elements and expected state changes.

questions.question: A popup opens in a new tab. Which approach reliably identifies the new tab without assuming handle order?
options: Switch to the second item returned by the handle set.
Compare the handles before and after opening, then switch to the newly added handle.
Close the original tab before checking handles.

questions.question: A Grid request requires Firefox on Linux, but the only registered node supports Chrome on Windows. What is the expected result?
options: Grid silently changes the requested browser to Chrome.
Grid changes the user-agent string and reuses the Windows node.
No matching node can serve the requested capabilities, so the session cannot be created until capacity/configuration changes.
The request runs locally on the test client automatically.

questions.question: Two parallel tests share a static WebDriver and intermittently type into each other’s forms. What is the best correction?
options: Give each test thread its own driver session and isolate its test data.
Make the shared driver field final.

questions.question: A file upload works locally but fails on a remote Grid node because the file exists only on the test runner. What should the setup do?
options: Pass the local path and assume the node shares the runner’s disk.
Transfer the file to the remote browser/node or use accessible shared storage.
Replace the file input with an alert.
Disable upload assertions during remote runs.

questions.question: The target input is inside an iframe nested within another iframe. Which sequence is required?
options: Switch directly to the inner frame from top-level content.
Switch to the outer frame, then locate and switch to the inner frame.
Switch to the alert, then to the inner frame.
Use Actions to hover over both frames.

questions.question: A Page Object constructor performs a payment and asserts that the payment succeeded. Which design is preferable?
options: Keep page operations in the Page Object and assert the business outcome in the test.
Keep all business assertions in the constructor so every test inherits them.
Move all locators into a static global class and remove test assertions.
Remove the assertions because Page Objects should verify all outcomes.

questions.question: An Appium test can inspect a hybrid app’s native controls but cannot locate its web elements. What should it investigate?
options: Whether web elements need to be found using native-only locators.
Whether it must switch to a discoverable WebView context and whether WebView debugging is configured.
Whether Appium capabilities can be changed after session creation to change the platform.
Whether the app’s database has a primary key.

questions.question: Mid-session, a test attempts to change the Appium platformName capability from Android to iOS. Which statement is correct?
options: Any capability can be changed whenever the test needs it.
Only platformName can be changed during a session.
Capabilities establish session parameters; changing platform requires creating an appropriate session.
Capabilities are used only by Selenium Grid, not Appium.

questions.question: A mobile test must preserve app data between Appium sessions. Which capability intent is most relevant?
options: Use noReset behavior where supported, understanding that it prevents the usual app reset.
Use fullReset because it preserves installed data.
Use platformVersion to preserve app storage.
Use automationName to disable app lifecycle handling.

questions.question: A native system permission dialog appears during an Appium test. Why may treating it as an ordinary web alert fail?
options: Native dialogs are always stored in the app’s database.
Web alerts can only appear on iOS.
A system dialog is outside the ordinary web DOM/alert context and may require platform-appropriate native interaction.
Selenium cannot automate any mobile UI.

questions.question: A mobile locator based on screen coordinates breaks when the same flow runs on a different display size. Which improvement is generally best?
options: Prefer stable accessibility identifiers or platform resource identifiers.
Disable orientation changes in all test environments.

questions.question: A TestNG DataProvider runs several invocations in parallel, and each updates the same account record. Failures are nondeterministic. What is the main issue?
options: TestNG automatically rolls back the shared record.
The invocation count is too low.
Parallel invocations share mutable test data; isolate records or serialize conflicting work.

questions.question: A prerequisite TestNG test fails, causing a dependent test to be skipped. Cleanup still needs to run. What is the strongest design?
options: Put cleanup in another test that depends on the failed test.
Put cleanup in an appropriate configuration method and use alwaysRun where suitable.
Give cleanup a lower priority number.

questions.question: A TestNG test logs a SoftAssert failure but still passes. What was most likely omitted?
A retry analyzer makes an intermittent test pass on its third attempt. What should the quality report do?
options: Hide earlier failures because the final attempt passed.
Remove the test from future runs.
Record the retries and investigate the flaky behavior; retries are not a fix.
Disable assertions on the first attempt.

questions.question: Two TestNG tests depend on one another and modify shared state, but the suite runs methods in parallel. What is the safest decision?
options: Assume dependency settings make shared state thread-safe.
Use isolated data or explicitly serialize the dependent workflow.
Convert the assertions to soft assertions.

questions.question: A Maven command uses mvn clean test -DskipTests. Which behavior is generally expected?
options: Clean and compile the project, but do not execute tests.
Skip compiling and executing tests, then deploy.
Skip the clean phase and package the project.

questions.question: A team wants Maven to skip compiling test sources as well as running tests. Which option is generally intended for that?
Two transitive Maven versions conflict at different depths. What is the usual dependency mediation rule?
options: Generally select the nearest definition; declaration order breaks equal-depth ties.

questions.question: What does invoking the Maven verify phase generally do in the default lifecycle?
options: Run only validation and stop before compilation.
Run only tests and skip earlier phases.
Execute the lifecycle phases up through verify, including earlier phases such as test, unless configured otherwise.
Deploy the artifact to a remote repository automatically.

questions.question: A production source imports a library declared with Maven test scope. What is the likely result?
options: Production compilation fails because a test-scoped dependency is not on the main compile classpath.
Maven silently changes the dependency to compile scope.
The library is always available in production.
Surefire removes the import before compilation.

questions.question: What is the most reliable way to compare two boxed Integer values when their numeric equality matters?
options: Use ==; all boxed values are cached.
Convert them to strings and compare object references.

questions.question: A custom object is used as a HashMap key. After insertion, a field used in its hashCode() changes and lookup fails. Why?
options: HashMap permits only immutable strings as keys.
The changed hash-relevant state can make the key’s current bucket inconsistent with its insertion bucket.
HashMap changes keys only after iteration.

questions.question: A catch block for IOException appears before a catch block for FileNotFoundException. The compiler rejects the code. Why?
options: FileNotFoundException is not related to IOException.
The broader catch makes the later, narrower catch unreachable.

questions.question: A service uses StringBuilder as a shared object modified by several threads. Which statement is most relevant?

StringBuilder makes all surrounding code thread-safe.
Java automatically creates a separate builder per thread.

questions.question: A superclass reference points to an object of a subclass that overrides an instance method. Which implementation normally runs?
options: The subclass override, selected using the object’s runtime type.
The superclass method, selected only by the reference’s declared type.
Neither unless the reference is cast.

options: GROUP BY cannot be used after joins.
Foreign keys remove all duplicate rows automatically.
Each account may repeat for every matching transaction; aggregate at the intended grain or count distinct account IDs.

questions.question: A transfer transaction debits the source account, but crediting the destination fails and the debit remains committed. What is the strongest expected behavior for an all-or-nothing transfer?
